newsitem.title: PERU: Red Cross says electricity off at Peru siege site.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross says electricity off at Peru siege site.

text.p: A generator supplying electricity to the Japanese ambassador's home where Marxist rebels were holding about 340 hostages has run out of fuel, leaving the residence without power, the international Red Cross said on Saturday evening.
"Fuel for the generator ran out about an hour ago. There is no more electricity for the moment," Red Cross official Jean-Pierre Sherra told reporters.
Sherra said the absence of power at the luxury residence, "could place general security in danger."
Electricity, water, telephone and cellular communications have been cut off at the ambassdor's home since Thursday. The generator had been used as a stop-gap measure in the meantime.
President Alberto Fujimori's government has not answered repeated pleas from hostages for services to be reconnected.
Sherra said the lack of power could delay further hostage releases by the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas who stormed the residence on Tuesday night.
"There will not be any more releases for the moment today as far as we know," he said.
Rebels have freed over more than hostages, including 38 on Friday night, since the crisis began.

The leader of the MRTA rebels, Nestor Cerpa, said in a walkie-talkie conversation with the local America Television station earlier on Saturday that more of their captives would gradually be released. This would not include those with ties to the government, he added.
